clue.text: He wanders right past

parts.note: over can mean past or finished, as in 'the danger is over'

explanation.surface: A man strolls by, keeping to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is someone who roams from place to place without a fixed home.

clue.text: Alexander and Frederick, for example, reading Classics at Oxford

definitions.meaning: both kings were called 'the Great'
The Oxford name for the honours course in Classics

explanation.surface: Someone studying ancient history at Oxford, reading about famous conquering kings.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander the Great and Frederick the Great are history's 'greats'; at Oxford University, the Classics degree (Literae Humaniores) is traditionally called Greats.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous rulers given the title 'the Great' are greats, and Oxford calls its Classics honours course by the same name.

clue.text: An examination at Scotland Yard which provides conclusive proof

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is based at Scotland Yard, London police headquarters
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Detectives at police headquarters run an examination that settles a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, home of its CID (detective branch). The examination there is a CID TEST, preceded by A.
explanation.definitionFit: The acid test, originally a way of telling real gold, is any trial that gives a decisive result.

clue.text: British advertising chap promotes a distinguished Australian batsman

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, so it stands for advertising
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A British ad executive is used to promote a famous Australian cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Don Bradman was Australia's greatest cricket batsman. 'promotes' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald Bradman, with a Test batting average of 99.94, is the most celebrated Australian cricketer.

clue.text: Disorder in a famous York street

definitions.meaning: a scene of chaos or mess
a medieval street in the city of York, England

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out on one of York's well-known historic streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shambles, a narrow medieval lane of overhanging timber buildings in York, takes its name from the old word for meat stalls or a slaughterhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete mess is a shambles, and the same word names York's old butchers' street.

clue.text: Doesn't our cook serve fine beef?

indicators.note: to cook something is to fiddle or rearrange it, as with cooking the books, so these letters get mixed up

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the kitchen will be serving a quality steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' looks like part of the restaurant question, but it is the anagram signal: DOESNTOUR (from 'Doesn't our', apostrophe ignored) is rearranged. 'serve' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a small round fillet steak, an expensive cut usually served in French cooking.

clue.text: Dad has a criminal conviction which could be aired on Radio!

definitions.text: which could be aired on Radio

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a criminal record is a list of past convictions, so record stands in for conviction

explanation.surface: Father is revealed to have a police record.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shameful family secret, but the definition is a single that a radio station plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart single by a popular-music act is what DJs play on the radio.

clue.text: Budding gun enthusiasts like to do so

definitions.meaning: a plant's new growth is said to be sprouting or putting out buds

definitions.text: gun enthusiasts like to do so
definitions.meaning: people fond of guns like to fire them, at game or targets

explanation.surface: Young aspiring gun lovers enjoy going out to fire at targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budding' looks like it means aspiring, but it points to a plant's new growth; the rest describes firing guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A young plant growth is a shoot, and firing a gun is shooting.

clue.text: They're handy weapons

definitions.meaning: the limbs that end in hands
weapons collectively

explanation.surface: A remark that guns and other weapons are useful to have nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Our upper limbs carry the hands, and military weaponry is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Men dared to break out, but were put back in custody

indicators.note: breaking out suggests escaping from a fixed arrangement, so the letters of these two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Prisoners attempted a jailbreak but were caught and returned to their cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break out' fits the prison story but signals that MENDARED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent back into custody by a court while awaiting trial is being remanded.

clue.text: Make a comment about German currency

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
the Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to say something about Germany's money.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something in passing or observe aloud is to remark.

clue.text: A female winner of the men's singles at Wimbledon

definitions.text: winner of the men's singles at Wimbledon

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a female

explanation.surface: A woman somehow wins the men's tennis title at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately absurd: a woman winning the men's event. The winner is Arthur Ashe, the American who won the Wimbledon men's title in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe took the gentlemen's singles crown at the All England Club in 1975.

clue.text: Rating got to the bottom of the mystery and was acquitted

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

parts.words: got to the bottom of the mystery
parts.note: to get to the bottom of a mystery is to have solved it

explanation.surface: A sailor cracks the case and is cleared of the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is an ordinary sailor in the Royal Navy; AB (able-bodied seaman) is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absolved is to be freed from blame or guilt, as a court frees a defendant.

clue.text: Intolerant admission from one confined to hospital

definitions.meaning: unwilling to wait or put up with delay

definitions.text: admission from one confined to hospital
definitions.meaning: split as two words, it is what someone kept on a ward might confess: that they are a person under medical care

explanation.surface: A hospitalised person confesses to being short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split I'M PATIENT, it is what someone on a hospital ward would admit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and unable to wait calmly is impatient; split, the word is a hospital inmate's statement.

clue.text: Many set out to gain a political pardon

indicators.note: out signals the letters are taken out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A large group set off to win pardon for political prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like 'set out' as in depart, but it is the anagram signal for MANYSET. 'to gain' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An official general pardon, often given to political offenders, is an amnesty.

clue.text: It ebbs and flows smoothly as darkness is falling

parts.note: even means level or smooth, so it stands for smoothly
the sea's tide ebbs and flows twice a day

explanation.surface: The sea moves gently in and out as night descends.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a time phrase: 'at eventide' means as darkness is falling.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, the time when night comes on.

clue.text: Soldier poet shortly to join elite military force

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is Britain's elite special forces regiment
soon means shortly

explanation.surface: A war poet is about to enlist in the special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service. 'to join' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried Sassoon was a decorated First World War officer famous for his war poetry.

clue.text: Came in as needing treatment for loss of memory

definitions.note: noun phrase for an adjective: the answer describes someone suffering from it

indicators.note: something in need of treatment is not in a fit state, signalling these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient arrived at the clinic seeking help for forgetfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing treatment' belongs to the medical story but signals rearranging CAMEINAS. 'for' links to the definition, which is loose: the answer means one suffering memory loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone affected by amnesia, the inability to recall the past, is amnesiac.

clue.text: Early childhood, and where it may be imagined

definitions.meaning: the first years of a person's life
split as two words, it says '...', that is, only in the imagination

explanation.surface: Early childhood, and imagining it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split IN FANCY, it is where something exists only as imagined.
explanation.definitionFit: Babyhood and the first years of life are a person's infancy; split, the word means 'in the imagination'.

clue.text: What one should do with Christmas decorations on January 6th? Put it in writing

definitions.text: What one should do with Christmas decorations on January 6th
definitions.meaning: tradition says festive decorations must be removed by Twelfth Night or bad luck follows
to record something on paper, as with dictation or notes

explanation.surface: Advice to remove the Christmas decorations at Epiphany and to note this down.
explanation.walkthrough: January 6th is Twelfth Night or Epiphany, the end of the Christmas season in British tradition, when decorations are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing decorations from walls is taking them down, and writing something on paper is also taking it down.

clue.text: Lady's fingers given approval by artist

parts.note: OK means approval, as in 'give it the OK'
RA, Royal Academician, is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter approves a woman's slender fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady's fingers' sounds like hands but is another name for the vegetable. 'given' and 'by' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, a green pod vegetable, is commonly called ladies' fingers in Britain and India.

clue.text: Noisy meal

parts.note: a slang word for food that sounds like the noise of someone chewing loudly

explanation.walkthrough: The slang word for food, from Yiddish, has a sound suggestive of loud eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: He copied out a translation in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places one piece within the outer one

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East of England, SE
a crib is a literal translation used by students, often illicitly

explanation.surface: A man made a handwritten copy of a translation somewhere near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South-East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Before printing, a scribe was employed to copy manuscripts by hand.

clue.text: Evelyn Waugh's novel is a sensational piece of journalism

definitions.meaning: Waugh's 1938 satire on Fleet Street war reporting
an exclusive story beating rival papers

explanation.surface: Evelyn Waugh's book is praised as remarkable reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh's comic novel Scoop satirises newspaper foreign correspondents.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive news story is a scoop, which is also the title of Waugh's newspaper satire.

clue.text: Her importance in the nursing world is relative

definitions.text: Her importance in the nursing world
definitions.meaning: a senior ward nurse in British hospitals holds the rank with this title
a female sibling is a family relation

explanation.surface: A nurse's high standing in hospitals is only a matter of comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a Sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward. 'is relative' sounds like 'is a matter of comparison' but means a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior ward nurse in Britain carries the title Sister, and a female sibling is a family member.

clue.text: It summarises what modern painting often is

definitions.meaning: a short summary of an article or paper
non-representational, as in much twentieth-century art

explanation.surface: A summary of the fact that modern art tends to be non-figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief summary of a paper is an abstract, and art that avoids depicting real objects is abstract.

clue.text: Current device for producing a lyric poem

parts.note: a becomes an before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject

explanation.surface: A gadget, powered by electricity, that writes poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' means electric current, not up to date. 'for producing' links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode through which electric current enters a device.

clue.text: Album read by the boxing fan?

definitions.meaning: a book of blank pages for pasting in cuttings and pictures
a scrap is a fight, so a boxing fan might read a book of scraps

explanation.surface: A boxing enthusiast reads through a collection of keepsakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' is British slang for a fight, so the second definition is a pun: a book about scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A book for pasting in cuttings is a scrapbook; split, it is a book of fights.
